title: Lighthouse Hosted API Bundle PRD + Launch Ops Checklist
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary: This PRD defines the Lighthouse Hosted API Bundle: a minimal, developer-friendly set of hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) packaged and released as a single, opinionated product offering for customers migrating from ad-hoc model endpoints. Goal: reduce onboarding time for new customers, provide clear behavioral contracts across generation + embeddings + rerank, and ship observability and rollback primitives to meet enterprise SLOs.

Scope (in):
- Chat endpoint: multi-turn state support, streaming, function/tool calling shim, and structured output (JSON schema support).
- Completions endpoint: single-call generation with temperature/top_p controls and token-level streaming.
- Embeddings endpoint: batched and streaming embedding generation, deterministic model selection, cosine normalization option.
- Rerank endpoint: pairwise/document scoring and ranked-list support with deterministic tie-breaking.
- Unified auth, rate-limits, per-route quotas, per-token billing, and SDK examples (Python/JS).

Out of scope (for this bundle):
- Multimodal image-to-text or vision inference.
- On-prem installer; Private/VPC-specific network controls (handled by Private product).
- Advanced model-switch routing policies (deferred to Dedicated roadmap).

User scenarios:
- Startup dev wants predictable latency for chat features; uses Chat with streaming and KV cache.
- Search team replaces an expensive re-ranker service with Lighthouse Rerank to reduce upstream latency.
- Analytics team computes vector similarity using batched Embeddings with deterministic model pinning.

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile <= 300ms for short-completions (<=64 tokens) on hosted small models; streaming tail metrics monitored separately.
- Availability: 99.95% regional uptime for hosted endpoints in GA regions.
- Cost visibility: token-level cost breakdown surfaced in Console within 24 hours of usage.
- Backwards compatibility: changes to default sampling params must not change observable outputs for existing production customers without explicit opt-in.

API contract highlights:
- Stable route names: /v1/lighthouse/chat, /v1/lighthouse/completions, /v1/lighthouse/embeddings, /v1/lighthouse/rerank.
- Input schema: JSON body with explicit fields for conversation history (chat), prompt (completions), items (embeddings), and candidate_pairs (rerank).
- Streaming: chunked transfer for chat/completions; SSE and WebSocket examples included in SDK.
- Error model: structured errors with codes (RATE_LIMIT, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE, TIMEOUT, INPUT_VALIDATION).

Rollout strategy:
1) Internal dogfood — Redwood apps and early partners (7 days)
2) Gradual customer opt-in via console toggle and API header (25% of onboarding traffic, 10 days)
3) Open GA with migration playbook and forced compatibility guardrails (30 days monitoring)

Rollback and degraded-mode behavior:
- Automatic fallback to compatibility variant: if a runtime reports increased 5xx or latency above 2x SLO for 5 minutes, route 80% traffic to verified fallback model and 20% to primary for monitoring.
- Manual rollback: console switch that maps route to previous model version and preserves conversation session ids for chat with mapping TTL 12 hours.

Operational readiness:
- Runbooks: per-region runbook for model OOM, KV cache eviction, and prefix cache warm-up.
- Observability: token-level traces, model-version histogram, per-route p50/p95/p99, and prompt-set regression alerts.
- Incident SLA: P1 on-call within 15 minutes, P0 escalation to platform SRE within 5 minutes.

Acceptance criteria (see separate list): detailed pass/fail checks used by QA and SRE before GA enablement.
acceptance_criteria: Chat: multi-turn context preserved across streaming sessions for 95% of synthetic conversation flows (1000 test flows).
Chat: function/tool calling JSON payload correctly invoked for all supported tool signatures in the SDK examples.
Completions: token streaming sequence is strictly monotonic and reassembled by SDKs without missing tokens across payload fragmentation tests (simulate 10% packet loss).
Embeddings: batch endpoint returns vectors with cosine_normalize=true matching single-call baseline within 1e-4 L2 difference for 99% of items.
Rerank: scoring is deterministic given same model/version/seed and ranking stability measured across 1000 candidate sets at 99% stability.
API: response error codes conform to spec and rate-limit responses include X-RateLimit-* headers.
Performance: 95th percentile latency targets met in benchmark environment and verified with production-like traffic profile.
Security: KMS-integrated secret rotation validated in staging, and SSO-based access to Console gating controls tested end-to-end.
Telemetry: cost-by-token and per-route latency breakdowns available in Console and dashboard panels updated within 24 hours.
Compatibility: migration toggle (header + console) re-routes traffic without client changes and is documented in migration guide.
launch_checklist: Final PRD review and sign-off by Product, Eng, Design, and SRE (owners in comments).
Security review completion and formal approval from Security team (attach security memo).
SDKs: Python and JS packages published with examples and changelog entries.
Runtime: dedicated canary cluster seeded and smoke-tested with scripted workloads.
Canary: 7-day dogfood with internal apps, monitor regressions and collect prompt-set quality metrics.
Migration docs: migration playbook + example curl commands published to Confluence and Console help center.
Observability: dashboards created and alerting thresholds validated (pager tests run).
Billing: per-token billing rules validated in staging and invoices simulated for a sample tenant.
Support: runbook snippets and FAQ prepared for Customer Support and Solutions Engineering.
GA enablement checklist: console toggle ready, opt-in rollout schedule approved, communications plan drafted.
monitoring_playbook: Alert: p95 latency deviation > 2x baseline across region -> page SRE and trigger automated fallback.
Alert: model 5xx rate > 0.5% over 5 minutes -> failover to fallback model, set incident priority P1.
Regression detection: weekly prompt-set A/B eval jobs with quality delta > 2% triggers release hold.
Cost spike detection: token cost per minute increases > 30% -> notify platform cost ops and throttle noncritical lanes.
